title: Replicating Safety Scores Under Decoding Parameter Variation
original_idea: Evaluate two models on HELM Safety at five temperature settings. Compute how safety scores change with temperature and identify hazard categories most sensitive to temperature.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Production deployments use varying temperatures. If safety degrades at higher temperatures, benchmark scores at temperature=0 systematically overestimate deployment safety. Strong practical implication.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Running HELM Safety requires setup of the evaluation framework. Varying temperature is simple but running full benchmark evaluations at five settings for two models is compute-intensive. Moderate complexity.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Two models, five temperatures, one benchmark. Clear parametric sweep. Well-defined deliverable. Feasible with medium compute in 30 hours.

novelty.reasoning: The effect of temperature on safety has been noted in safety evaluation literature. S-Eval (arXiv:2405.14191, 2024) acknowledges that fixed decoding parameters like temperature 0.7 may not capture nuances of safety performance. Research has shown increasing temperature and top-p leads to decreased safety. SORRY-Bench (ICLR 2025) addresses safety evaluation methodology. However, a systematic parametric sweep — two models, five temperature settings, one benchmark (HELM Safety), with per-hazard-category sensitivity analysis — has not been published as a focused empirical study. The general direction (temperature affects safety) is known, but quantifying which hazard categories are most temperature-sensitive on a standard benchmark is a useful and partially novel contribution.

evidence: S-Eval: Automatic and Adaptive Test Generation for Safety Evaluation. arXiv:2405.14191, 2024.
SORRY-Bench: Systematically Evaluating Large Language Model Safety Refusal Behaviors. ICLR 2025.
HELM Safety Evaluation Framework. Stanford CRFM, 2024.
